name: Direct Debit Setup and First Collection
orchestration_notes: DDI setup is initiated by the channel (PER-001 via mobile/web) or by the originator via AUDDIS. SVC-009 (Domestic Payments, CAP-003) owns the DDI and collection lifecycle. Cross-capability coordination with CAP-001 (account balance check and debit) is exclusively via async events through SVC-102. No direct API calls cross capability boundaries.
sca_method: FIDO2/WebAuthn biometric or TOTP for customer-initiated DDI setup via digital channel. AUDDIS originator-initiated flows do not require real-time SCA but are validated against the customer's account details.

phases.name: DDI Setup
phases.description: Customer authorises a Direct Debit Instruction (DDI). Three setup channels exist: (1) Customer completes a paper mandate provided by the originator — the originator submits via AUDDIS; (2) Customer sets up the DDI online through the bank's digital channel (mobile or web), authorising the instruction via SCA; (3) Originator initiates directly via AUDDIS (Automated Direct Debit Instruction Service), submitting the mandate to the bank as paying PSP. In all cases, a DirectDebitInstruction entity (ENT-034) is created by SVC-009 with status = pending, capturing the originator SUN (Service User Number), account details, and BACS reference.
persona_actions: Customer reviews Direct Debit mandate details: originator name, amount type (fixed or variable), estimated first collection date
Customer confirms authorisation — for digital channel: completes SCA (FIDO2 biometric or TOTP)
Customer receives confirmation that the Direct Debit mandate has been submitted for setup
system_actions: For customer-initiated (digital channel): channel calls SVC-009 POST /direct-debits with account_id, originator_sun, originator_name, reference, amount_type, first_collection_date
For AUDDIS-initiated: SVC-009 receives AUDDIS 0N instruction from BACS infrastructure; creates DirectDebitInstruction (ENT-034) with status = pending
SVC-009 creates ENT-034 (DirectDebitInstruction) with status = pending
SVC-009 publishes DirectDebitInstructionCreated (EVT-069)
SVC-103 creates WORM audit log entry for mandate creation
phases.exit_condition: DirectDebitInstruction (ENT-034) created with status = pending; EVT-069 published
nfr_references: API response < 2,000ms P99 for digital channel initiation

phases.name: DDI Validation
phases.description: SVC-009 validates the DDI against the bank's account records and AUDDIS scheme rules. Validation checks: (1) Sort code and account number belong to an active account (SVC-001 queried via CAP-001 Retail Banking API — within-capability synchronous call is permitted since SVC-009 and SVC-001 are co-located in the payment processing plane; however for cross-capability separation, SVC-009 publishes an event and awaits AccountDetailsConfirmed); (2) Customer identity matches the account holder (name matching); (3) Originator SUN is registered and active in the BACS scheme; (4) No duplicate active DDI exists for the same originator SUN + reference combination. If validation passes, the DDI is forwarded to BACS via AUDDIS for scheme-level registration.
persona_actions: No customer action required during this phase
Customer may receive an informational notification that their DDI is being processed
system_actions: SVC-009 validates sort code/account number against BACS scheme modulus checking
SVC-009 calls CAP-001 API to confirm account is active and account holder name matches (cross-capability: implemented as event-driven request-reply pattern via SVC-102)
SVC-009 validates originator SUN against BACS scheme directory
SVC-009 checks for duplicate active DDI (same originator_sun + reference)
If all checks pass: SVC-009 submits AUDDIS 0N (new instruction) to Vocalink/BACS infrastructure
SVC-009 publishes DirectDebitInstructionValidated (EVT-070)
If validation fails: SVC-009 updates DirectDebitInstruction.status = cancelled with rejection_reason, publishes appropriate rejection event, and notifies customer via SVC-053
phases.exit_condition: DirectDebitInstruction validated; EVT-070 published; AUDDIS 0N submitted to BACS
governance_references: Pay.UK BACS Participation Rules — AUDDIS scheme
nfr_references: Validation < 5 seconds; AUDDIS submission within T+0 of instruction receipt

phases.name: DDI Confirmation
phases.description: BACS confirms successful registration of the DDI. SVC-009 receives BACS confirmation (ADDACS notification for amendments/confirmation, or implicit acceptance after the AUDDIS 0N submission window). The DirectDebitInstruction is updated to status = active and a BACS reference is assigned. The customer is notified of the active mandate. The Direct Debit Guarantee (indemnity claim rights) is disclosed to the customer at this point as required by BACS scheme rules.
persona_actions: Customer receives confirmation notification: mandate is active, originator name, amount type, first collection date, and BACS reference
Customer is presented with the Direct Debit Guarantee summary (their indemnity claim rights)
Customer can view and manage their active Direct Debits in the account management section
system_actions: SVC-009 receives BACS ADDACS confirmation or records successful AUDDIS 0N acceptance after scheme processing window
SVC-009 updates DirectDebitInstruction.status = active; records bacs_reference
SVC-009 publishes DirectDebitInstructionValidated (EVT-070) if not already published, or updates status and emits confirmation signal
SVC-053 dispatches DDI confirmation notification to customer: originator name, amount type, first collection date, BACS reference, Direct Debit Guarantee summary
SVC-103 records mandate activation in WORM audit log
phases.exit_condition: DirectDebitInstruction.status = active; BACS reference assigned; customer notified with Direct Debit Guarantee disclosure
governance_references: BACS Direct Debit Guarantee — paying PSP disclosure obligation
nfr_references: Customer notification dispatched within 1 business day of BACS confirmation

phases.name: First Collection Submission
phases.description: The originator (utility company, subscription provider, etc.) submits the first collection instruction via BACS, 2 working days before the collection date (D-2). SVC-009 receives the BACS collection file (pmt.002 or equivalent BACS DDI debit instruction), validates it against the active DirectDebitInstruction, and creates a DirectDebitCollection entity (ENT-035) with status = submitted. The customer can view the pending collection in their account management view.
channel: BACS (External Scheme) — no customer channel interaction
persona_actions: Customer may view pending Direct Debit collection in the upcoming transactions section of the digital channel (D-2 visibility)
Customer cannot cancel the collection at this stage without cancelling the mandate and claiming under the DD Guarantee
system_actions: SVC-009 receives BACS Direct Debit file from Vocalink/BACS infrastructure (originator-submitted collection instruction at D-2)
SVC-009 validates collection: matches active DirectDebitInstruction (ddi_id), amount is consistent with amount_type (fixed amounts must match; variable amounts must be within agreed parameters)
SVC-009 creates DirectDebitCollection entity (ENT-035) with status = submitted, collection_date = D+0, submission_date = D-2
SVC-009 publishes DirectDebitCollectionSubmitted (EVT-071)
SVC-053 dispatches advance notice notification to customer (amount, collection date, originator name) — Consumer Duty best practice
SVC-103 records collection submission in WORM audit log
phases.exit_condition: DirectDebitCollection (ENT-035) created with status = submitted; EVT-071 published; advance notice sent to customer
governance_references: Consumer Duty advance notice best practice
nfr_references: Collection file processing < 2 hours of BACS file receipt

phases.name: Collection Processing
phases.description: On the collection date (D-0), SVC-009 initiates the debit. SVC-009 cannot directly debit the customer account — cross-capability coordination with CAP-001 (Retail Banking) is required. SVC-009 publishes DirectDebitCollectionSubmitted (EVT-071) or a dedicated DirectDebitDebitRequested event consumed by SVC-001. SVC-001 checks the available balance and, if sufficient, debits the account and publishes AccountDebited. If insufficient funds, SVC-001 returns a funds-unavailable signal and SVC-009 returns the collection to BACS with reason code ARUDD (Automated Return of Unpaid Direct Debit). The DirectDebitCollection status is updated accordingly.
channel: No customer channel interaction during processing
persona_actions: Customer sees debit appear in their transaction feed (post-debit)
If insufficient funds: customer sees a notification that their Direct Debit was returned unpaid, with advice on consequences
system_actions: SVC-009 publishes cross-capability event on D-0 to trigger account debit (consumed by CAP-001/SVC-001)
SVC-001 consumes event: checks available balance against collection amount; if sufficient, debits the account ledger
SVC-001 publishes AccountDebited event (cross-capability, consumed by SVC-009 via event bus)
SVC-009 consumes AccountDebited: updates DirectDebitCollection.status = collected
SVC-009 publishes DirectDebitCollectionProcessed (EVT-072)
SVC-053 dispatches post-debit notification to customer
SVC-103 records collection outcome in WORM audit log

If insufficient funds: SVC-001 publishes InsufficientFundsSignal (via event bus); SVC-009 creates ARUDD return instruction; updates DirectDebitCollection.status = returned with return_reason = insufficient_funds; publishes DirectDebitCollectionReturned (EVT-073); SVC-053 notifies customer of unpaid Direct Debit
phases.exit_condition: DirectDebitCollection.status = collected (happy path) or returned (insufficient funds); EVT-072 or EVT-073 published
nfr_references: Account debit processing < 4 hours of BACS D-0 settlement window opening

phases.name: Indemnity and Disputes
phases.description: The customer may dispute a Direct Debit collection under the Direct Debit Guarantee at any point. The DD Guarantee gives the customer an unconditional right to an immediate full refund from their bank for any payment taken in error. The bank must credit the account immediately on the customer's indemnity claim, then recover the amount from the originator via the BACS indemnity claim process. SVC-009 manages the indemnity claim lifecycle.
persona_actions: Customer contacts the bank (digital channel, branch, or telephone) to claim under the Direct Debit Guarantee
Customer identifies the disputed collection: originator name, amount, date
Customer submits indemnity claim — no evidence or justification required under the DD Guarantee
system_actions: Channel (or branch staff) calls SVC-009 POST /direct-debits/{ddi_id}/indemnity-claim with collection_id, claimed_amount, claim_reason
SVC-009 validates the claim: collection must be an active or recent DirectDebitCollection record
SVC-009 publishes DirectDebitIndemnityClaimFiled (EVT-074)
SVC-001 consumes EVT-074 (cross-capability via event bus): credits the claimed_amount to the customer account immediately
SVC-001 publishes AccountCredited event
SVC-009 initiates INDEMNITY claim instruction to BACS to recover from originator
SVC-009 updates DirectDebitCollection.status = indemnity_claimed
If customer wishes to cancel the mandate: SVC-009 cancels the DirectDebitInstruction (AUDDIS 0C — cancellation instruction to BACS), updates status = cancelled
SVC-053 dispatches indemnity confirmation notification to customer: credited amount, mandate cancellation status
SVC-103 records indemnity claim outcome in WORM audit log
phases.exit_condition: IndemnityClaimFiled (EVT-074) published; account credited; BACS indemnity claim submitted to originator; customer notified
governance_references: Direct Debit Guarantee — paying PSP immediate refund obligation

happy_path.description: Customer authorises a DDI online via digital channel. AUDDIS registration succeeds. BACS confirms the mandate. Originator submits first collection at D-2. Balance is sufficient at D-0. Account debited successfully. Customer receives transaction confirmation.

timing_breakdown.ddi_setup_to_active: T+1 to T+3 working days (AUDDIS processing cycle)
timing_breakdown.account_debit: D-0 (collection date, within BACS settlement window)

alternative_paths.name: Paper Mandate / Originator-Initiated AUDDIS
alternative_paths.description: Customer completes a paper mandate with the originator. The originator submits via AUDDIS directly to the bank's BACS infrastructure. PH-046 begins with AUDDIS 0N receipt by SVC-009 rather than a digital channel API call. No SCA required (originator is the initiating party). Bank still notifies customer on DDI activation (PH-048).

alternative_paths.name: Variable Amount Direct Debit
alternative_paths.description: DirectDebitInstruction.amount_type = variable. Originator submits different amounts for different collections. Validation at PH-049 checks that the amount is within any agreed parameters. Customer receives advance notice of each collection amount at D-2 (Consumer Duty best practice for variable DDs).
governance_references: Consumer Duty — advance notice for variable amounts

alternative_paths.name: Customer Cancels DDI Before First Collection
alternative_paths.description: Customer cancels the Direct Debit Instruction via digital channel before the first collection is processed. SVC-009 cancels the DirectDebitInstruction (status = cancelled), submits AUDDIS 0C (cancellation) to BACS, and notifies the originator. No collection is processed.

exception_paths.name: AUDDIS Validation Failure — Invalid Account Details
exception_paths.description: BACS returns an AUDDIS rejection: sort code/account number combination does not match the paying bank's records, or the account is not eligible for Direct Debits (e.g. savings account, closed account). SVC-009 updates DirectDebitInstruction.status = cancelled with rejection_reason = invalid_account_details. Customer and originator are notified.
exception_paths.trigger: BACS AUDDIS rejection code received by SVC-009
exception_paths.customer_message: Your Direct Debit for [originator] could not be set up. Please contact [originator] to update your account details.

exception_paths.name: Insufficient Funds — Collection Returned Unpaid
exception_paths.description: On D-0, the account has insufficient funds to cover the collection. SVC-001 cannot complete the debit. SVC-009 returns the collection to BACS with ARUDD code (Automated Return of Unpaid Direct Debit). The DirectDebitInstruction remains active unless cancelled. The originator may re-present the collection. Customer is notified and may face charges from the originator.
exception_paths.trigger: SVC-001 balance check fails at D-0 collection processing
exception_paths.customer_message: Your Direct Debit to [originator] for £[amount] could not be collected on [date] due to insufficient funds. Your Direct Debit arrangement remains in place. Please ensure your account has sufficient funds for future collections.
exception_paths.internal_action: ARUDD return instruction submitted to BACS. DirectDebitCollection.status = returned. Customer notified. DirectDebitInstruction.status unchanged (remains active).
governance_references: Consumer Duty — clear customer communication on unpaid DDs

exception_paths.name: Customer Indemnity Claim — DD Guarantee
exception_paths.description: Customer disputes a collection under the Direct Debit Guarantee. Bank must credit the account immediately and unconditionally. Covered in full in PH-051.
exception_paths.trigger: Customer contacts bank to claim under DD Guarantee
exception_paths.customer_message: Your indemnity claim of £[amount] from [originator] has been credited to your account immediately under the Direct Debit Guarantee.

design_decisions.decision: Cross-capability coordination between CAP-003 (SVC-009 Domestic Payments) and CAP-001 (SVC-001 Retail Banking) for the D-0 account debit is implemented exclusively via async events on SVC-102 (Event Bus). SVC-009 does NOT call SVC-001 directly.
design_decisions.rationale: The architecture principle 'cross-capability communication is exclusively async events' applies here. SVC-009 (CAP-003) and SVC-001 (CAP-001) are in different capability domains. SVC-009 publishes an event requesting the account debit; SVC-001 processes it and publishes AccountDebited in response. This decouples payment operations from retail banking and prevents tight coupling of the BACS processing engine to the ledger service.

design_decisions.decision: The DirectDebitInstruction (ENT-034) is owned by SVC-009 (CAP-003), not SVC-001 (CAP-001), despite the account being owned by SVC-001.
design_decisions.rationale: The DDI is a BACS scheme artefact governed by CAP-003 (Payment Operations — BACS Processing sub-capability). The DDI lifecycle (AUDDIS submission, validation, activation, collection, indemnity) is entirely within the payment operations domain. SVC-001 is only involved for balance checks and debit execution. Placing ENT-034 in CAP-003 maintains clean capability boundaries.

design_decisions.decision: For the indemnity claim (PH-051), the account credit is triggered by SVC-001 consuming EVT-074 (DirectDebitIndemnityClaimFiled) asynchronously. The bank's obligation under the DD Guarantee is to credit 'immediately' — the async event processing must complete within a customer-observable near-real-time window (< 30 seconds) to meet this obligation.
design_decisions.rationale: The DD Guarantee requires immediate credit — this is a regulatory obligation, not a best-effort SLA. The event-driven architecture must guarantee processing latency below customer perception thresholds. SVC-001's consumer group for the topic payments.direct-debit must have low-latency processing priority configured.

design_decisions.decision: A single API contract covers all CAP-003 Direct Debit operations (payment-operations.openapi.json). There is no separate per-service API contract for SVC-009.
design_decisions.rationale: Per the architecture rule: API contracts are per-capability, not per-service. CAP-003 is the capability boundary exposed to consumers (channels). SVC-009 is an internal implementation detail of CAP-003. The capability API (payment-operations.openapi.json) is the published surface.
